title: model-specific runtime optimizations: Llama/Mistral/Qwen quirks + GQA/MQA tuning
author: Diego Martinez
description:
Motivation: Several production customers observed suboptimal latency/throughput for Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants under mixed-quantized workloads. Root causes included: suboptimal kernel selection heuristics for short vs long sequence paths, incorrect rotary/rope handling for Mistral leading to extra compute, KV-cache fragmentation for Qwen's custom KV layout, and conservative GQA/MQA parameter defaults that reduced throughput on GPUs.

Summary of changes: 1) Kernel selector: introduce model-aware heuristics (architecture + sequence-length histogram) to prefer fused attention kernels for Llama when seq_len < 512 and switch to block-attention for long contexts. 2) Mistral rotary fix: correct rotary indexing when using per-layer rotary scales -> eliminates extra transpose and reduces memory traffic. 3) Qwen KV layout: add compacted KV cache path and reworked memory stride to align KV tensors to 128B which removes expensive memcopies on some GPUs. 4) GQA/MQA tuning: expose new quantization profiles and per-model defaults (gqa_profile and mqa_profile) tuned for throughput on A100/H100; also improved quantization-dequantization kernel fusion to reduce CPU-GPU synchronization. 5) Scheduler improvements: continuous-batching policies now respect model-specific min-batch-time and allow partial-batch flush thresholds for low-latency p99 control. 6) KV cache compaction API: safe background compaction to reduce fragmentation on long-lived sessions.

Benchmarks (internal, synthetic traffic similar to prod): - Llama-2-13B (8-bit, seq=128): +26% throughput, -18% p95 latency. - Mistral-7B (fp16, seq=2048): -12% p95 latency on long-context workloads due to rotary fix and reduced transposes. - Qwen-7B (gqa, mixed-quant): +14% throughput, 20% lower peak GPU memory for high-concurrency workloads. - End-to-end served throughput (mixed fleet, 1000 concurrent reqs): +11% overall.

Compatibility and rollout: Changes are backwards compatible by default. New quantization profiles are off by default for existing deployments; rollout plan: dark-launch profiles to 10% traffic -> monitor perf and quality -> gradual enabling via rollout policies. KV compaction runs off by default and must be enabled per-deployment.

Testing: Added unit tests for rotary index calculations, integration tests for KV layout paths, and a perf canary that exercises the continuous-batching thresholds. CI includes new microbenchmarks; a perf job gate was added to avoid regressions.

Notes: This PR focuses on runtime-side changes only (no model weights). A follow-up will add CLI docs and console toggles in the Redwood Console for the GQA/MQA profiles.
